title: Spring Lecture #13: Spring Boot CRUD Project with Soft Delete

questions.question: What happens to the student's row in MySQL when the lecture's soft delete API is called, compared with hard delete?
options: Both remove the row; soft delete just does it later in a background job
Soft delete moves the row to a separate `deleted_students` table; hard delete removes it
Soft delete keeps the row and sets its deleted flag to true; hard delete removes the row permanently
Soft delete clears all columns except the id; hard delete removes the row
questions.explanation: Soft delete only updates one field (`deleted`/`isDeleted` = true) so the record stays in the table but is hidden from normal APIs, while hard delete (`deleteById`) removes the row. The lecture does not move or blank any data: the full row remains, which is what makes soft-deleted data recoverable.

questions.question: Why does the lecture expose soft delete as `PATCH /api/students/delete-soft?id=1` instead of using `DELETE`?
options: Because soft delete only changes one field of an existing record, which is a partial update, and PATCH is meant for partial updates
Because browsers cannot send DELETE requests, so PATCH is used as a workaround
Because PATCH automatically restores the record after 30 days
Because DELETE requests cannot carry a query parameter such as `id`
questions.explanation: The notes reason that soft delete is technically a partial update (only `isDeleted` changes), so PATCH fits; DELETE is reserved for the API that actually removes the row. DELETE requests can carry query parameters, as the lecture's own hard-delete endpoint `/delete?id=` shows.

questions.question: The `student` table has these rows: (1, Rahul, deleted=false), (2, Priya, deleted=true), (3, Aman, deleted=false). What does `GET /api/students/getAll` return?
options: 200 OK with Rahul, Priya and Aman
200 OK with only Priya
404 Not Found, because one of the rows is deleted
200 OK with Rahul and Aman
questions.explanation: Spring Data derives `... where deleted = false` from `findByDeletedIsFalse`, so only the two active students are returned and the list is non-empty, giving 200. Returning all three would be the behaviour of `findAll()`, which ignores the soft-delete flag.

questions.question: The lecture's entity names the flag `private Boolean deleted;` (getter `getDeleted()`). A student copies a method name from the notes, which used a field called `isDeleted`. Which repository method makes the application fail at startup?
options: `List<Student> findByDeletedFalse();`
`List<Student> findByIsDeletedFalse();`
`List<Student> findByDeletedIsFalse();`
`Optional<Student> findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse(Long id);`
questions.explanation: Derived queries are built from entity property names: in `findByIsDeletedFalse`, the property part is `IsDeleted`, and `Student` has no property `isDeleted`, so creating the repository fails with a property-not-found error. `False` and `IsFalse` are both accepted keywords, so `findByDeletedFalse` and `findByDeletedIsFalse` are valid, and `IdAndDeletedIsFalse` combines two valid conditions.

questions.question: Priya (id 2) was soft deleted and correctly disappears from `/getAll`. But QA reports that `GET /api/students/get?id=2` still returns Priya with 200. The service's `getStudent` calls `studentRepository.findById(id)`. What is the fix?
options: Change the controller mapping from `@GetMapping` to `@PatchMapping`
Call `deleteById(2L)` so the row is also physically removed
Use `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse(id)` in `getStudent`, since `findById` returns any existing row regardless of the flag
Add `@Column(name = "is_deleted")` so `findById` starts filtering deleted rows
questions.explanation: `findById` only matches the primary key, and a soft-deleted row still exists, so it is returned. The notes introduce `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse`/`findByIdAndIsDeletedFalse` exactly for get-by-id APIs. `@Column` only renames the column and adds no filtering, and hard-deleting would defeat the purpose of soft delete.

questions.question: Student 1 is active. Postman sends `PATCH /api/students/delete-soft?id=1` twice in a row. What are the two responses?
options: 200 "Record deleted", then 404 Not Found
200 "Record deleted" both times
404 Not Found both times
200 "Record deleted", then 500 because the row is already deleted
questions.explanation: The first call finds the active student, sets `deleted=true` and saves, returning 200. On the second call `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse(1L)` finds nothing because the flag is now true, so the service returns false and the controller sends 404. No exception occurs; the empty Optional is handled explicitly.

questions.question: Student 3 was soft deleted. The admin then calls the hard delete API `DELETE /api/students/delete?id=3`, which checks `existsById(id)` before `deleteById(id)`. Why does this call succeed with 200?
options: Because hard delete first restores soft-deleted rows and then deletes them
Because `deleteById` only works on rows whose deleted flag is already true
Because the controller ignores the result of `existsById` for DELETE requests
Because `existsById` only checks the primary key; the soft-deleted row still exists, so it returns true and the row is removed
questions.explanation: Built-in JpaRepository methods like `existsById`, `findById` and `findAll` know nothing about the soft-delete flag: the row is physically present, so `existsById(3L)` is true and `deleteById` removes it. Only custom derived methods such as `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse` filter on the flag.

questions.question: The table already had 50 students before you added `private Boolean deleted;` to the entity. With `ddl-auto=update`, Hibernate added the new column, and new students are created with `setDeleted(false)`. Now `/getAll` returns only the students created after the change. Why?
options: `ddl-auto=update` deleted the old rows when it altered the table
The old rows have NULL in the new column, and `deleted = false` is not true for NULL, so `findByDeletedIsFalse` skips them
`findByDeletedIsFalse` only returns rows inserted after the repository method was declared
Hibernate caches the first 50 rows and never returns them again
questions.explanation: `update` adds the column without deleting data, but existing rows get NULL for it, since no value was ever set. In SQL, `NULL = false` is not true, so the derived `where deleted = false` filters those rows out. That is why the notes initialise the field (`private Boolean isDeleted = false;`) and the code sets it on create; old rows need a one-time `UPDATE ... SET deleted = false`.

questions.question: You need a new API that returns only the active (not soft-deleted) students of a given subject. Following the lecture's "findBy + fieldName + condition" convention, which repository method declaration is correct for the `Student` entity (fields `subject`, `deleted`)?
options: `List<Student> findBySubjectAndDeletedIsFalse(String subject);`
`List<Student> findByDeletedIsFalseSubject(String subject);`
`List<Student> findAllWhereSubjectAndNotDeleted(String subject);`
`List<Student> findBySubjectDeletedFalse(String subject, Boolean deleted);`
questions.explanation: Each condition is a property name plus an optional keyword, and conditions are joined with `And`, exactly like `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse`. `Subject` takes the method parameter while `DeletedIsFalse` needs none. The other names either miss the `And` connector, use words that are not property names, or add a parameter that no condition consumes, so Spring Data cannot derive a query from them.

questions.question: An admin wants to undo the soft delete of student 2. Since the lecture's `updateStudent` ends with `studentToSave.setDeleted(false)`, they call `PUT /api/students/update?id=2` with the full student body. What happens?
options: The student is restored, because `updateStudent` always sets `deleted` to false
A new active copy of student 2 is inserted with a new id
The update succeeds but `deleted` stays true, because `setDeleted` is ignored by `save()`
404 Not Found: `updateStudent` looks the student up with `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse`, which finds nothing, so `setDeleted(false)` never runs
questions.explanation: The service returns null as soon as `findByIdAndDeletedIsFalse(2L)` is empty, and the controller turns null into `ResponseEntity.notFound()`. The `setDeleted(false)` line is only reached for students that are already active, so it cannot restore anyone; a restore feature would need its own lookup (e.g. `findById`) and endpoint.
